design: Three causes put every engine module into one shared chunk, not one. (1) worker.ts spread the engine namespace. (2) Challenge.svelte called await import('@engine'), and Rolldown then put every engine module into that dynamic entry's chunk _astro/src.*.js. This is why RT-FIX-P3-perf-b saw no change on '/'. (3) The bundler treated the engine's modules as having side effects, so an import through index.ts reached them all. Fixes: worker.ts imports the engine only as a type (import type * as Engine), so EngineApi is the same type. engineCall's signature and its E-9 routing (ALWAYS_IN_WORKER, whereToRun) are unchanged, and the engineApi value export is gone. A new export, provide(fns: Partial<EngineApi>), fills the main-thread Map, which starts with positionsOf and firstForbiddenMove. I chose it over an optional argument because RT-FIX 5.5 counts an added optional parameter as a contract change. A name nobody provided still runs from the whole engine, loaded on demand through loadEngine: () => import('./engineAll') (export * from the engine, its own chunk engineAll.<hash>.js). A TypeError still rejects a name the engine lacks. When E-9 keeps such a call on the main thread, the name is recorded in __testing.fallbacks() and a development build warns in the console (the warning is not in the production build). In Node, a call routed to the worker is not reported. Callers provide in their own script with named imports: T1 play (as enginePlay) and raisingPlay; T4 orbitGraph; t09/playOn.ts raisingPlay; T10 orbitGraph and wythoffEdges; T12 chevalleySerre; T15 applyWord. playFate is never provided because E-9 always runs it in the worker. T11 calls only positionsOf, so it is unchanged, as are counter.ts, studio.ts, scene.ts, t11/model.ts and t12/model.ts (types and whereToRun only). Challenge.svelte now imports boardFromName and mutate by name. A lazy small module was measured too and cost about 0.6 kB per route. astro.config.mjs exports moduleSideEffects(id), false only for packages/engine/src/*.ts, and passes it as vite.build.rolldownOptions.treeshake.moduleSideEffects. The engine now splits into board (core), weyl, geometry, fold, wythoff, heaps and rep chunks. satake.ts and satakeCatalogue.ts are only in engineAll and the worker.

handoff: T13, T14 and later tools: import every engine function by name from '@two-games/engine' or '@engine'. Never use import * as, import('@engine') or export * of the engine in site/src; worker-provide.test.ts fails on them. A module that calls engineCall('<name>', ...) also calls provide({ <name> }) in its own script with that function imported by name, even when the hint sends the call to the worker; only playFate, positionsOf and firstForbiddenMove need no provide, and a call by a computed name provides every name it can take. Kind 'satake' runs on the main thread except on E7 and E8 or with expectedItems, so T13 must provide satake, satakeRecord and the rest of what it calls; otherwise its route falls back to the whole engine chunk and engine-fallback.spec.ts fails if that happens in a default state. engine-weight.spec.ts already lets routes with data-tool 'satake' or 'atlas' carry satake.ts and satakeCatalogue.ts. A new engine module must declare only, with no side effects at its top level. Specs must find engine code by content (site/tests/e2e/engineChunks.ts), never by a chunk name. For MERGE: the moduleSideEffects rule could move to "sideEffects": false in packages/engine/package.json (the owner's choice; I did not edit the engine). Keeping the fallback costs 0.2 to 3.0 kB per route (measured, recorded in the fragment).
